Synopsis:
    The Indian rupee posted a 10-week closing high driven by stronger-than-expected dollar inflows under an RBI special scheme, giving the central bank significantly more firepower to actively manage the currency in both directions. Near-term upside for the rupee is capped by importer dollar demand, elevated oil prices linked to renewed U.S.-Iran military tensions, and rising U.S. Treasury yields (~4.78%) with a ~63% probability of a Fed rate hike in September. Oil price inflation is widening India's import bill and reinforcing dollar demand from importers, while also feeding global bond yield pressure.
